newsitem.title: NEPAL: India-Nepal border talks end inconclusively.
newsitem.headline: India-Nepal border talks end inconclusively.

text.p: Officials from Nepal and India ended six days of talks on Tuesday without resolving a dispute over a small piece of land in western Nepal that has marred bilateral relations, officials said.
"The meeting could not take a decision on Kalapani," Nepali Foreign Secretary Kumar Gyawali told Reuters.
"The next meeting will be held in New Delhi and the dates will be decided through diplomatic channels," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

The dispute between landlocked Nepal and its giant southern neighbour arose last year after they signed a treaty to build a dam on the Mahakali river, which originates in Kalapani and forms Nepal's western border with India.
Nepal says the river's actual point of origin is located west of Kalapani where India has a security post. The Nepali claim implies that India should remove its post.
Officials said the dispute needed to be resolved before the two countries finalised a detailed project report for the 6,000 megawatt dam. The report is due to be completed by the end of 1997.
